text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I'll dive into the `/prompts/` directory and audit the top 10 most-used prompts by execution count in `usage_logs.json`. I'll run `grep -r "\"executions\": [1-9][0-9]*" . | sort -t: -k2 -nr | head -10` to identify them, then review each for redundancy or inefficiency. After that, I'll apply safe optimizations (e.g., consolidating similar prompts) and log the changes in `CHANGES.md`. Lead, let me know if you want me to prioritize specific prompt types.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Hold—your `grep` regex `"executions": [1-9][0-9]*` is a blunt instrument that misses prompts with *exactly* 100+ executions (e.g., `"executions": 100` fails the `[1-9]` prefix) and ignores JSON arrays or nested structures. Provide a corrected query *and* evidence that your audit scope covers all execution contexts (e.g., logs, DB, cache) before we greenlight this. Quality first—don’t let partial data mislead the review.
